Write down the call it blocks

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 3 "Agree the outcome" L29 "where the evidence run reads it" points forward at the next exercise (gather-the-evidence) without naming it; harm (an unresolvable referent stalling the reader) absent because the clause only says the file is read later and the action asked is complete without it. Also L7 "The doubt you just chose" and L21 "the same file" (./crux.md, named in chunk 1's prompt) resolve via module include order (read-the-digest picks the doubt) and the deck's prior slide.

L7 "The doubt you just chose" is the student's lived module beat, named by its content, not a positional file callback; L13 "the outcome you wrote on Day 1" names the artefact. No "the opening lecture"-type pointer in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L7 "the doubt you just chose" -> apt101-read-the-digest.md L72 (product owner writes the chosen doubt at the top of team/doubts.md), same module include order; L13 "the outcome you wrote on Day 1" -> team/bet.md produced by Day 1 exercises (grep team/bet.md hits apt101-choose-the-bet/what-goes-in/build-your-product-memory).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal beat; every chunk is a verbed instruction

rules_evaluated.evidence: Smallest chunk 3 "Agree the outcome" L29 carries a full self-sufficient instruction (agree, then four named file actions); chunk 0 L1-9 carries time, purpose and the three roles.

chunk 2 "Write down the call it blocks" L19-25 is exactly that: name the decision the obstacle blocks, append to file; chunk 3 header "Agree the outcome" matches L29 "Decide together"; chunk 1 L11-17 matches.

Closest: L9-L10 three consecutive "The X ..." role sentences (product owner, designer, team lead) - each leg carries new concrete content (drives; checks against customer words; checks actionability), so not an empty triple. No "Not X. Not Y. Z." in body (the "Not the outcome again" series sits in a prompt fence, exempt); no self-grading superlative; no number+retraction; no abstraction-noun stack.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep of body_numbered for beat|surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|mood -> 0 hits ("beat" appears only at L36 in maintainer block). "obstacle", "crux" (file name) and "opportunity tree" are training vocabulary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget - bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 0 L3 "**Time:**" and L5 "**What you do:**" - two bold labels, but they are the exercise template's fixed field labels (<=2 words), not bold lead sentences; chunks 1-3 carry no bold.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content - verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise is included in whats-actually-true.md L28 as a standalone [Exercise: ...] include, so it lands under a .phase--exercise wrapper; derive-body-view slide_count 3 plus the title chunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering - position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js | grep pick-the-outcome -> no output; headers L11, L19, L27 carry no hand numbers and body has no Phase/Step references.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js | grep pick-the-outcome -> no output. Closest: L29 "at the top of ./crux.md" locates inside a file, not on the page.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no in-body links; signals has_slide_includes false

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size - 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise headings L11 "Find what stands in the way", L19 "Write down the call it blocks", L27 "Agree the outcome" are all imperative phase labels; no declarative heading to test.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies - three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 2 L25 "Push back if the question is a topic (\"what about onboarding?\")" repeats the prompt's own example, but the second sentence adds the new test (a call one would stay late to make); not a doctrine restatement, self-referential commentary or kicker. Rewrite offered as suggestion only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: git log -p -3 on the file shows no +/- ## header line changes; each body answers its header.
